facts.statement: The genus Tholodus was first named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1851.
facts.quote: It was first named by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1851

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Tholodus schmidi.
facts.quote: the type species is Tholodus schmidi

facts.statement: Tholodus lived during the Middle Triassic, specifically from the mid-late Anisian to the late Ladinian stage.
facts.quote: Middle Triassic (mid-late Anisian to late Ladinian stage)

facts.statement: Fossils of Tholodus have been found in Germany, northeastern Italy, and possibly China.
facts.quote: Germany, northeastern Italy and possibly China

facts.statement: Most Tholodus specimens were collected from the Ladinian-aged Muschelkalk in Germany, mainly from the Jena Formation of the upper Lower Muschelkalk, where the holotype was discovered.
facts.quote: Most specimens were collected from various localities across the Ladinian-aged Muschelkalk, Germany, mainly from the Jena Formation of the upper Lower Muschelkalk, where the holotype was found

facts.statement: The humerus of Tholodus resembles that of immature individuals of the Asian genus Chaohusaurus, suggesting possible affinities to Grippidia.
According to Maisch (2010), the only difference between Tholodus and Xinminosaurus is that Tholodus specimens are on average twice as large as the Xinminosaurus holotype.
facts.quote: The only difference between the taxa, according to Maisch (2010), is that Tholodus specimens are at average twice as large as Xinminosaurus holotype

facts.statement: Tholodus belongs to the family Omphalosauridae.
Tholodus is classified within the order Ichthyosauria.
Tholodus is classified within the class Sauropsida.
The parent group of Tholodus is Omphalosauridae.
Tholodus is classified as a reptile.
Tholodus lived in the Middle Triassic (mid-Anisian to late Ladinian) in what is now Europe, particularly Germany, northwest Italy, and possibly China.
